candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity client-needs subcategory (6–12% of items); this item tests recognition of anxiety related to chronic illness, therapeutic communication, psychosocial assessment, coping support, and coordination of appropriate resources.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial assessment and symptom-management support for anxiety associated with chronic dyspnea
candidate.educational_objective: Address anxiety associated with chronic breathlessness as a legitimate component of respiratory illness by assessing it, reinforcing safe breathing/relaxation strategies, and coordinating psychological support while continuing appropriate medical evaluation and treatment.

options.A: Acknowledge the anxiety as part of the symptom experience, assess its severity and safety impact, reinforce appropriate breathing or relaxation strategies, and coordinate additional psychological support when needed
options.B: Tell the client that anxiety is unrelated to chronic breathlessness and should be ignored while respiratory treatment continues
options.C: Stop evaluation of the underlying respiratory condition because the symptoms are primarily psychological
options.D: Advise the client to avoid all physical activity permanently so anxiety about breathlessness cannot recur

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current American Thoracic Society resources describe anxiety as a common and clinically meaningful problem in chronic respiratory disease and note that breathlessness and anxious states can interact in maladaptive cycles. ATS emphasizes integrated, personalized care rather than separating psychological symptoms from respiratory care. Current ATS palliative-care guidance also identifies counseling for anxiety and difficulty breathing as a supportive intervention alongside medical treatment. B dismisses a legitimate psychosocial component. C creates a false psychological-versus-physical dichotomy and risks missing respiratory deterioration. D promotes unnecessary avoidance and deconditioning rather than individualized symptom management and appropriate activity.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current ATS resources directly support anxiety as a meaningful component of chronic respiratory illness, interaction between anxiety and breathlessness, and integrated psychological/breathing support alongside ongoing respiratory care.
candidate.source_document_title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to Manage Anxiety in Chronic Respiratory Disease; Palliative Care for People with Respiratory Disease or Critical Illness
candidate.source_locator: ATS 'Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to Manage Anxiety in Chronic Respiratory Disease' → 'The impact of anxiety in chronic respiratory disease': anxiety can exacerbate symptom severity; breathlessness is closely linked with anxious states; anxiety and breathlessness may contribute to maladaptive cycles of avoidance and deconditioning. 'Moving toward a stepped, multimodal approach': psychological support should be integrated into comprehensive respiratory management. ATS 'Palliative Care for People with Respiratory Disease or Critical Illness' → chronic lung disease examples: counseling may be used to help with anxiety and difficulty breathing while medical treatment continues.
candidate.source_version_date: Current ATS Pulmonary Rehabilitation Assembly educational resource and current ATS Patient Education palliative-care resource accessed 2026-08-18
